items.claim: The unit's own quoted closing verse is missing from its evidence-reference list, an internal citation gap unlike every other row in this stretch.
items.evidence: The messenger-formula onset and the shift from the preceding third-person remnant announcement to direct second-person address to Zion are solid grounds for the front boundary, and the koh-amar is correctly named as divine-frame rather than royal-messenger. But the rationale quotes its own argued close, “It will happen in that day that his burden will depart from off your shoulder, and his yoke from off your neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed because of the anointing oil.” (web:Isa.10.27), while the evidence-reference list stops at the opening formula and never carries that closing verse forward into it. Every other unit in this stretch -- the neighboring felling-oracle unit, whose internal hinneh-clause “Behold, the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will lop the boughs with terror. The tall will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low.” (web:Isa.10.33) sits just before its own close at web:Isa.10.34, the peaceable-kingdom close at web:Isa.11.9, the second-exodus close at web:Isa.11.16, the chapter close at web:Isa.12.6, the atrocity-scene close at web:Isa.13.16, and the desolation close at web:Isa.13.22 -- carries its own quoted closing verse into the evidence-reference list; this unit alone does not, leaving its back boundary's citation incomplete relative to the argument actually made in prose.

items.claim: Both boundaries carry genuine tier-1 warrant, and the internal hinneh-clause at the felling verse is named and defended rather than silently absorbed.
items.evidence: The front boundary marks a real shift from the direct second-person assurance oracle closing at web:Isa.10.27 to a third-person poetic report opening with the invader's approach by named place, “He has come to Aiath. He has passed through Migron. At Michmash he stores his baggage.” (web:Isa.10.28). The unit correctly treats the third-person hinneh-clause spliced from הִנֵּ֤ה הָאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.10.33, byte tier), “Behold, the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, will lop the boughs with terror. The tall will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low.” (web:Isa.10.33), as a real internal-seam candidate and gives an argued reason for keeping it inside the same unit -- that it resolves the same approaching-army scene rather than opening an unrelated one -- rather than passing over it in silence, which is the standard this whole stretch should be held to. The setumah marks falling inside and at the close of the span are disclosed as tier-3, single-witness corroboration, never as the driver of the boundary.

items.claim: The front boundary rests on a genuine new-subject onset, and the cross-seam echo with the preceding felled-forest image is disclosed rather than left silent.
items.evidence: A fresh grammatical subject enters at “A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.” (web:Isa.11.1), deliberately answering the felled-tree imagery of the immediately preceding unit; the rationale names this echo explicitly rather than leaving a byte-true straddling device undisclosed, and still draws the boundary at the new-subject onset, which is the correct tier-1 marker for the seam. The unit closes on the inclusio “the earth will be full of the knowledge of Yahweh, as the waters cover the sea.” (web:Isa.11.9), matching the owner-specified salvation_oracle example for this exact stretch, and the petuchah at the close is disclosed as tier-3, single-witness corroboration rather than as a driver.

items.claim: The named rejected alternative is not clearly the strongest rival: the verse's own nations/ensign scope continues the universal theme of the immediately preceding unit at least as strongly as it anticipates the regathering oracle that follows.
items.evidence: The formal rejected-alternative names only folding the verse forward into the regathering oracle, set aside because that oracle marks its own action as happening “the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” (web:Isa.11.11). But the verse's own content, “the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.” (web:Isa.11.10), continues the universal, all-peoples scope of the immediately preceding close, “the earth will be full of the knowledge of Yahweh, as the waters cover the sea.” (web:Isa.11.9), at least as plausibly as it anticipates the following unit's return of an ethnically particular remnant named from specific lands (web:Isa.11.11). The unit's own device notes concede this verse could equally be read as the closing coda of the preceding shoot-of-Jesse unit, but that reading is never adjudicated against the one actually named in the formal rejected-alternative field, leaving the stronger candidate rival undisclosed there even though the medium_low confidence itself is honestly held.

items.claim: The second-time marker is a genuine self-distinguishing tier-1 device opening a discrete regathering action, and the unit correctly resists splitting off the Judah/Ephraim material where no addressee shift marks it off.
items.evidence: The unit opens on the Lord's hand acting “the Lord will set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea.” (web:Isa.11.11), spliced from יוֹסִ֨יף אֲדֹנָ֤י שֵׁנִית֙ (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier), a self-referential marker distinguishing this regathering action from what precedes it. It closes on the second-exodus highway, “There will be a highway for the remnant that is left of his people from Assyria, like there was for Israel in the day that he came up out of the land of Egypt.” (web:Isa.11.16), at the chapter's own close, never cutting the chapter division. The rejected alternative correctly identifies that splitting off a separate reconciliation unit inside this stretch is unwarranted because no addressee shift or fresh onset marks that material off from the surrounding regathering promise.

items.claim: The Yah-plus-tetragrammaton short-form claim is stated as a categorical 'never blended' without the adjacent digit-bearing count the same device notes correctly supply for the twin-strophe claim beside it.
items.evidence: The device notes state the short-form stack spliced from יָ֣הּ יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.12.2, byte tier) is counted as its own site and 'never blended into the plain tetragrammaton census' -- a categorical claim carrying no adjacent digit naming how many such short-form sites are being set apart from that census. The same device notes supply the sanctioned digit-bearing form for the twin onset in the same unit, citing it as a two-verse sweep; the short-form claim is held to a looser citation standard than the row's own twin-onset claim two sentences away. The underlying seam logic is otherwise sound: both strophes, “In that day you will say,” (web:Isa.12.1) and “In that day you will say,” (web:Isa.12.4), share the same speaker, addressee, and doxological register, and the unit correctly closes “Cry aloud and shout, you inhabitant of Zion, for the Holy One of Israel is great among you!” (web:Isa.12.6) at the frame boundary without crossing into the following oracle collection.

items.claim: The formal rejected alternative addresses only the front-seam superscription question and never names the more proximate internal rival: a second hinneh-clause inside this same span, structurally identical to the one this stretch elsewhere treats as a live internal-seam candidate.
items.evidence: The span quietly absorbs a third-person hinneh-clause opening its own sub-scene, spliced from הִנֵּ֤ה יוֹם יְהוָה֙ בָּ֔א (oshb:Isa.13.9, byte tier), “Behold, the day of Yahweh comes, cruel, with wrath and fierce anger; to make the land a desolation, and to destroy its sinners out of it.” (web:Isa.13.9) -- a construction of the same form as the hinneh-clause this same writing stretch elsewhere treats as a genuine internal-seam candidate requiring explicit disclosure and an argued reason to keep it unified rather than silent absorption. Here no such disclosure appears and no rival naming this candidate is offered anywhere in the row. The formal rejected-alternative field instead argues only against making the header a fourth stand-alone superscription row 'alongside Isa.1.1 and Isa.2.1' -- but naming only two precedents while calling a third addition beside them 'a fourth' is an internal count mismatch within that same sentence. The header-fusion conclusion itself is sound and correctly keeps the massa Bavel header fused with its content rather than isolating it as a superscription row, and the frame boundary at the M1/M2 seam is correctly respected on both sides of the join.

items.claim: The hinneh-plus-named-agent onset is a genuine tier-1 scene shift, distinguishable in kind from the internal hinneh-clauses this same oracle otherwise absorbs, and the unit correctly keeps the header-bounded oracle's unit type.
items.evidence: The first-person divine hinneh-clause naming a specific historical agent, spliced from הִנְנִ֛י מֵעִ֥יר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אֶת מָדָ֑י (oshb:Isa.13.17, byte tier), “Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, who will not value silver, and as for gold, they will not delight in it.” (web:Isa.13.17), introduces a genuinely new subject not previously named in the governing oracle, unlike the third-person hinneh-clauses elsewhere in the same Babylon burden that continue an already-established scene without introducing a new agent; the shift to first person plus a newly named actor is the stronger tier-1 marker. The unit correctly keeps its unit type tied to the still-governing massa header at web:Isa.13.1 rather than treating the new agent as grounds for a fresh header classification, and it closes “Hyenas will cry in their fortresses, and jackals in the pleasant palaces. Her time is near to come, and her days will not be prolonged.” (web:Isa.13.22) before the causal addressee shift to Jacob opens the following unit.
